Two additional points beyond the feedback above:

1. Every current test and validator expects YES, so a program that only prints YES passes the entire suite without checking the number. Add negative cases early in both sets: N = 1 (proper-divisor sum 0), a prime such as 13 (sum 1), 8 (sum 7), and 12 (sum 16). The last two cover sums below and above N, so both must return NO.

2. The Constraints section is empty. Please specify the supported range of N and ensure both the input and divisor-sum intermediates fit the intended integer type. The existing 137438691328 case already requires more than 32 bits.

These changes would make the numeric contract explicit and ensure the tests actually distinguish perfect from non-perfect numbers.
